title: INC-2026-002: Macro-enabled document leads to PowerShell loader and DLL beaconing on Finance workstation WS-FIN-022
severity_rationale: Host compromise with attacker code execution and repeated outbound contact to an attacker domain is confirmed on WS-FIN-022 (user m.okafor). The host was isolated and reimaged. No confirmed exposure of sensitive data at scale: EDR shows no internal connections in 24h, but domain controller logs were not reviewed and data impact is unknown.
executive_summary: A macro-enabled document from the internet was opened on WS-FIN-022 by m.okafor, and Word then launched hidden, encoded PowerShell. PowerShell fetched a script from cdn-update.badcdn.test, dropped upd.dll and ran it with rundll32. That process then contacted the same domain repeatedly, which probably indicates command-and-control. The Finance OU was exempt from the macro-blocking policy, which is the root cause. The attachment's delivery path (for example email) is not confirmed. EDR on Finance workstations was detect-only and the email gateway does not sandbox .docm files, so nothing stopped the chain. The high-severity EDR alert sat in the queue from 08:47 until 11:15 because of analyst backlog. The host was isolated at 11:22. The host was reimaged and the hashes and domain were blocked. Data impact and lateral movement are not confirmed because domain controller logs have not been reviewed.

what_happened.statement: User m.okafor opened Invoice_Oct.docm in Word on WS-FIN-022. The file carried an internet mark-of-the-web.
About 20 seconds later WINWORD.EXE spawned PowerShell with hidden-window, no-profile, encoded-command arguments. EDR raised high-severity alert EDR-3301 but only detected, not blocked.
PowerShell connected to cdn-update.badcdn.test and retrieved s2.ps1 (HTTP 200, about 18 KB inbound).
PowerShell wrote upd.dll to the user's AppData\Roaming folder, then launched it via rundll32.exe.

rundll32.exe made repeated small HTTPS requests to cdn-update.badcdn.test/api/c at 08:49 and 08:50, and again at 11:21, just before isolation. This pattern is consistent with command-and-control beaconing, but the proxy logs do not show what the traffic contained.
A SOC analyst picked up EDR-3301 at 11:15. The alert had waited in the queue since 08:47 amid a backlog of 40 alerts and two analysts on shift.

evidence.excerpt: Alert had been in the queue since 08:47

what_happened.statement: WS-FIN-022 was isolated via the EDR console at 11:22. Both file hashes and the domain were blocked at EDR and proxy at 11:40. The host was reimaged and returned to the user the next day.

evidence.excerpt: Isolated WS-FIN-022 from the network via EDR console
Blocked both file hashes and cdn-update.badcdn.test
WS-FIN-022 reimaged and returned to m.okafor

what_happened.statement: EDR shows no connections from WS-FIN-022 to other internal hosts in the last 24h. Domain controller logs had not been reviewed at the time of the ticket.

attack.rationale: The user opened a macro-enabled Office document from the internet, and Word then spawned PowerShell.
PowerShell was launched with an encoded command and fetched a remote script.
PowerShell was run with a hidden window.
A script was pulled from an external host, and a DLL was then written to disk by PowerShell.
The dropped DLL was executed via rundll32.exe.
rundll32 made repeated small HTTPS requests to an attacker domain, consistent with web-protocol C2 beaconing.

immediate_cause.statement: The user opened an internet-sourced macro-enabled document (Invoice_Oct.docm), after which Word launched PowerShell. The macro executing is inferred from the Word-to-PowerShell process chain.

evidence.excerpt: the attachment looked like a real supplier invoice

root_cause.statement: The whole Finance OU was excluded from the policy that blocks macros in files from the internet (added in 2024 for a legacy Excel add-in), so the macro document could run.

evidence.excerpt: the Finance OU is excluded from the policy that blocks macros in files from the internet
Exclusion added in 2024 for a legacy Excel add-in

contributing_factors.statement: EDR on Finance workstations is in detect-only mode, so the Office-to-PowerShell launch was not blocked.

evidence.excerpt: EDR policy on Finance workstations is detect-only

contributing_factors.statement: The email gateway does not sandbox .docm attachments. Whether this document arrived by email is not confirmed.

evidence.excerpt: the email gateway does not sandbox .docm attachments

contributing_factors.statement: The lure looked like a genuine supplier invoice, which made it more likely to be opened.

evidence.excerpt: the attachment looked like a real supplier invoice

data_affected.statement: Not determined. Outbound byte counts in the proxy rows are small, but the evidence does not state what data, if any, was accessed or taken from the workstation.

operational_impact.statement: WS-FIN-022 was isolated, then reimaged and returned to the user the next day.

evidence.excerpt: WS-FIN-022 reimaged and returned to m.okafor

business_impact.statement: Financial or business cost is not stated in the evidence.

detection_gaps.statement: The high-severity alert EDR-3301 waited in the queue from 08:47 until 11:15 because of a 40-alert backlog and two analysts on shift. Beaconing continued to 11:21.

evidence.excerpt: Alert had been in the queue since 08:47

detection_gaps.statement: EDR was detect-only on Finance workstations, so the alert had no automatic blocking effect.

evidence.excerpt: so the PowerShell launch was not blocked

detection_gaps.statement: Scoping is incomplete: domain controller logs were not reviewed.

evidence.excerpt: Domain controller logs not reviewed yet

lessons.lesson: Exclusions to the macro-blocking policy must be narrow (signed macros or trusted locations). Excluding a whole OU for a legacy add-in left a standing gap for 2024 onwards.

evidence.excerpt: Exclusion added in 2024 for a legacy Excel add-in

lessons.lesson: Detect-only EDR on high-value Finance endpoints turned a blockable Office-to-PowerShell chain into a multi-hour compromise.

evidence.excerpt: EDR policy on Finance workstations is detect-only

policy_refs.title: EDR mode
policy_refs.excerpt: Detect-only mode is allowed only during a rollout of at most 14 days.

lessons.lesson: Macro-enabled attachments should be sandboxed or quarantined before reaching users.

evidence.excerpt: the email gateway does not sandbox .docm attachments

policy_refs.title: Email attachments
policy_refs.excerpt: are detonated in a sandbox before delivery or quarantined

lessons.lesson: A high-severity alert waited in the queue for hours behind a backlog. The 2025 post-incident review already recorded that alerts waiting behind higher-severity ones delay response, so queue prioritisation and capacity remain a recurring weakness.

policy_refs.title: Lessons
policy_refs.excerpt: waited behind higher alerts for 40 minutes

lessons.lesson: Scoping must include authentication and domain controller review before closure, as the playbook requires. It was still open at the time of the ticket.

evidence.excerpt: Domain controller logs not reviewed yet

policy_refs.title: Scoping
policy_refs.excerpt: Review domain controller and authentication logs for the user and host

corrective_actions.recommendation: Remove the Finance OU exclusion from the macro-blocking policy. If the legacy Excel add-in is still needed, allow only signed macros or specific trusted locations.
corrective_actions.reason: The OU-wide exclusion is the root cause; it allowed an internet-sourced macro document to run.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: the Finance OU is excluded from the policy that blocks macros in files from the internet

corrective_actions.expected_benefit: Macro-based initial execution is blocked on Finance workstations.

corrective_actions.recommendation: Switch EDR on Finance workstations to prevent (block) mode, and audit all other hosts for detect-only configurations beyond the 14-day rollout allowance.
corrective_actions.reason: Detect-only mode meant the PowerShell launch was alerted on but not stopped.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: EDR policy on Finance workstations is detect-only

corrective_actions.expected_benefit: The Office-to-PowerShell chain is blocked at execution instead of only alerted on.

policy_refs.title: EDR mode
policy_refs.excerpt: EDR runs in prevent (block) mode on all workstations and servers.

corrective_actions.recommendation: Enable sandbox detonation or quarantine of .docm/.xlsm attachments at the email gateway.
corrective_actions.reason: The gateway does not sandbox .docm attachments, and this document looked like a legitimate invoice.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: the email gateway does not sandbox .docm attachments

corrective_actions.expected_benefit: Malicious macro documents are stopped or flagged before reaching users.

policy_refs.title: Email attachments
policy_refs.excerpt: Macro-enabled Office attachments (.docm, .xlsm) are detonated in a sandbox before delivery or quarantined.

corrective_actions.recommendation: Complete scoping: review domain controller and authentication logs for m.okafor and WS-FIN-022 and check for credential theft and lateral movement. Search all endpoints for the two hashes and the domain.
corrective_actions.reason: Domain controller logs were not reviewed, and EDR evidence alone shows no internal connections. The ticket does not record an enterprise-wide search for the indicators.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: Domain controller logs not reviewed yet

corrective_actions.expected_benefit: Confirms or rules out spread and credential exposure before the incident is closed.

policy_refs.title: Scoping
policy_refs.excerpt: check for lateral movement and credential theft before closing the incident

policy_refs.title: Blocking
policy_refs.excerpt: search all endpoints for the same indicators

corrective_actions.recommendation: Raise the priority of alerts for Office applications spawning PowerShell or other process-chain alerts, and add queue-age escalation so high-severity alerts are not left for hours. Review SOC staffing against alert volume.
corrective_actions.reason: A high-severity alert sat for over two hours during a backlog while beaconing continued. The earlier agreed action on alert triage and prioritisation was not enough to prevent this.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: Alert had been in the queue since 08:47

corrective_actions.expected_benefit: Shorter time from alert to analyst action and containment.

policy_refs.title: Lessons
policy_refs.excerpt: triage alerts for the same user together

open_questions: How did Invoice_Oct.docm reach the user (email, web download or other)? No email delivery is recorded, so phishing is not confirmed.
Did the macro itself run? This is inferred from the Word-to-PowerShell process chain and is not directly shown.
What did the beaconing and the downloaded script do, and was any data accessed or taken from WS-FIN-022? The EDR export does not say.
Do domain controller and authentication logs show credential use or lateral movement from WS-FIN-022 or m.okafor?
Do other endpoints, especially in the Finance OU, show the same hashes or contact with cdn-update.badcdn.test? The ticket does not record an enterprise-wide search.
Were other Finance users sent the same document?
remaining_risks: Other Finance OU hosts remain exempt from macro blocking and in detect-only mode until the policies are changed.
Possible credential exposure or lateral movement cannot be ruled out until domain controller logs are reviewed.
Other recipients of the same lure, if any, are not accounted for.
